vocab.definition: one that will run out, e.g. crude oil, metal ores.
one that is replaced as fast as it is used.
a material from the Earth, sea or air.
meets our needs without harming the future.

misconceptions.right: Many (oil, ores) are finite and will run out.
Man-made materials can outperform natural ones.
It means using resources wisely for the future.

infoPanels.title: FINITE vs RENEWABLE
workedSteps: Sustainable development = balance need and future.
Reduce, reuse and recycle to conserve resources.

questions.text: State what is meant by a finite resource. [1 mark]
Classify each as finite or renewable: crude oil, wood, copper ore. [3 marks]
Explain what is meant by sustainable development. [2 marks]
Suggest how chemistry helps make resources last longer. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: A ______ resource will ______, while a renewable one is replaced.

questions.text: Suggest one benefit and one drawback of using a renewable resource. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Finite = will run out; renewable = replaced as fast as it is used.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why is recycling metals more sustainable than extracting new ore?
